requires.label: Patient must be a Colorado resident
requires.quote: An individual must be a Resident of Colorado in order to qualify for Financial Assistance

rules.label: Income-based assistance: FPL <= 250%
rules.quote: Patients approved for Financial Assistance with an annual Family Income of 250% of FPL guidelines or less will receive a 100% discount on gross charges for care covered by this policy

rules.label: Income-based assistance: FPL 251-400%
rules.quote: Patients approved for Financial Assistance with an annual Family Income between 251% and 400% of FPL guidelines will receive a discount on gross charges as outlined in Appendix A

rules.label: Presumptive Eligibility
rules.quote: Patients granted Presumptive Eligibility for Financial Assistance will receive a 100% discount on gross charges for care covered by this policy

application.quote: 365 days from the date of the first post-discharge Billing Statement

eca_not_before.quote: UCHealth will refrain from initiating ECAs for at least 365 days from the date the Hospital mails the first post-discharge Billing Statement

notes: Residency exception: For unscheduled emergency services, UCHealth may, at its sole discretion, make an exception to the residency requirement.
Services not covered: elective or cosmetic surgery; transplant procedures; self-pay packages; single case agreements; grants & research; services with a legal obligation for a third party to pay.
Provider coverage varies by facility; a separate Provider List (updated quarterly) identifies which physicians are covered.
Family definition: group of two or more related by birth, marriage, or adoption residing together; family members not responsible for patients age 18+.
Financial Resources definition: cash, bank deposits, or assets easily withdrawn without penalty (checking, savings, trusts, CDs).
AGB (Amount Generally Billed) caps charges for FAP-approved patients; AGB percentages vary by facility and FPL band (see Appendix A tables).
If self-pay discount at a facility exceeds AGB, the self-pay discount is applied instead.
Presumptive eligibility only applies to current services and past accounts, not future services.
UCHealth does not report patient debt to credit agencies nor place liens on patient property.
ECAs include legal action and wage garnishment; contracted collection agencies must follow this policy.
Income verification documents required (pay stubs, bank statements, tax returns, etc.) but are procedural, not eligibility criteria.
Application processing: completed applications processed within 14 days; written determination provided.
Eligibility validity periods: 365 days for FPL <= 250%; 180 days for FPL 251-400%; re-application required after expiry.
Incomplete applications denied but ECAs paused; applicant gets written notice of missing info and reasonable opportunity to complete within application period or 30 days of notice.
If approved after ECAs initiated, UCHealth reverses ECAs and refunds excess payments (except $1 or less).

Billing statements: at least 4 monthly statements mailed every 30 days; itemized statements provided within 10 business days of request, 30 days after discharge for inpatients, or 30 days after service for outpatients (whichever is later).
Collections referral: insured balances unpaid 120+ days; uninsured balances unpaid 182+ days; if no action 365 days from first statement, ECAs may initiate.
UCHealth employees residing outside Colorado but receiving services at UCHealth facility do not have to meet residency requirements.
Patients with UCHealth debt are not denied services for non-emergency care and not excluded from financial assistance.
UCHealth does not deny discounted care on basis patient has not applied for public benefits programs.
Non-cash benefits (food stamps, housing subsidies) excluded from Family Income calculation.
Predictive model using public record data may be used for presumptive eligibility when estimated household FPL <= 250%.
req-residency may leave out a condition: policy allows discretionary exception for emergency services

dropped.quote: Health care services that are not emergent or Medically Necessary, including elective or cosmetic surgery
